entry.note: Confirmed book is 'Vorlesungen über das Ikosaeder und die Auflösung der Gleichungen vom fünften Grade' by Felix Klein, 1888 (282 pages, archive.org/details/vorlesungenber00kleiuoft). Index entries include §142 'Die Bring'sche Form', §192 'Classification der Curven und Flächen', §207 'Die Bring'sche Transformation', §189 'Die Hauptresolvente der Ikosaedergleichung'. The QOU citations in magic-numbers-bring.{md,lean} for (1) S_5-stable sub-lattice classification and (2) Bring's curve as unique genus-4 with maximal S_5 — both covered by Klein's icosahedron-and-quintic book.

relevance.rationale: BROKEN SOURCE JOIN: the named file does not exist in the tree and no scan corresponding to this id is present under uploads/. Identity unconfirmable from front matter. Citation sites: zero .md prose; three .ts cites arrays (klein-bring-icosahedral-bridge.ts:19, magic-numbers-bring.ts:16, n-v-bring-action.ts:6) and four .lean files. Load-bearing assessment splits in two. (a) brings-surface/klein-bring-icosahedral-bridge.lean:120 cites it for the icosahedral quotient identity P^1/A_5 = S^2(2,3,5), which is squarely the subject matter of the cited work and is plausible. (b) lean/QOU/Conjectures/MagicNumbersBring.lean:29 attributes to it a classification of S_5-stable sub-lattices on Bring's curve. That attribution is doubtful on its face: the cited work is about the icosahedron, A_5 and the solution of the quintic, not about S_5-stable sublattices on Bring's curve, which is later literature. observations/magic-numbers-bring.lean:21 already records the pointer as unverified. This is a candidate cited-for-a-claim-it-does-not-support and needs the source, or a different reference, before conj:magic-numbers-bring leans on it.

proposedActions.rationale: Record that the S_5-stable-sublattice attribution at MagicNumbersBring.lean:29 is unverified against the cited work, whose subject is the icosahedron/A_5 and the quintic; the S_5 action on Bring's curve needs a separate source. Scope-(a): as read from the corpus alone the attribution is unsupported, not disproved.
